extracted.intended_audience: partners, donors, governments, and civil society organisations (CSOs) interested in Gavi programmes and funding
extracted.subtask_short: gavi programme priorities and funding criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Gavi's programme areas, strategic priorities, and specific funding mechanisms (e.g., CSO grants) that guide which activities and actors Gavi supports. Useful for prospective applicants, partners and policy stakeholders seeking to align proposals with Gavi priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall scope of Gavi's work
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work spans vaccine support, strengthening health systems, making immunisation sustainable and shaping vaccine markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the high-level priorities against which Gavi designs programmes and funding: vaccine delivery/support, health system strengthening, sustainability, and market interventions. (Page presents these as the organising pillars; each has its own programme pages.)

rubrics_metrics.name: The Gavi Leap (organisational transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming the Vaccine Alliance for the future through simplicity, transparency and synergy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as an organisational transformation priority — emphasises simplification, transparency and synergies across activities. Applicants/partners should align to these principles where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our vaccine portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Gavi supports vaccines against 20 infectious diseases, including Ebola, malaria, mpox and rabies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the disease and vaccine scope Gavi prioritises. Proposals targeting vaccines or vaccine-preventable diseases within this portfolio are most aligned with Gavi's programme focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthening health systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong health and immunisation systems are vital to deliver vaccines to all the children who need them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals emphasis on investments that build system capacity (supply chain, workforce, service delivery) to reach all children — particularly relevant for proposals that aim to improve delivery and access rather than only procure vaccines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gavi funding for civil society organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: A funding mechanism providing grants for CSOs working to reach zero-dose children and missed communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a targeted grant mechanism for civil society organisations focused on reaching zero-dose and missed populations — major cue for CSOs to design proposals explicitly targeting these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market shaping
rubrics_metrics.description: Working to improve the health of markets for vaccines and other immunisation products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects Gavi's role in interventions that influence vaccine markets (e.g., pricing, supply, supplier diversification). Relevant for proposals or partners aiming at market-level interventions rather than only programmatic delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our impact (performance against strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since its creation in 2000, Gavi has helped vaccinate over 1 billion children in the world’s poorest countries, preventing more than 17.3 million future deaths. Learn about how we've performed against our strategic goals, the independent…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to Gavi's emphasis on measurable impact and accountability — applicants should expect rigorous monitoring of outcomes and alignment with strategic goals and independent evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 6 (2026–2030) / Gavi 6.0 strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: In June 2024, the Board approved Gavi’s new five-year strategy, ‘Gavi 6.0’. Gavi 6.0 sets out the Alliance’s vision, mission, strategic goals, objectives, operating principles and critical enablers for Gavi’s sixth strategic period (2026–2030).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the current strategic framework that will guide funding decisions and programme priorities during 2026–2030. Proposal alignment with Gavi 6.0's goals and operating principles will be important for fundability.
